Introduction Farm with SolarNow (FASO) is a 4-year project that has been implemented by SolarNow under the Netherlands Embassy Food Security Cluster Program. The project officially started on 15 November 2018 as a 2-year project, and has been extended for an additional 2 years until 15 November 2022. Through an end-user contribution program, SolarNow primed the market for agricultural equipment by providing 1,026 farmers with access to modern agricultural productive technologies over the 4 year project period, contributing to enhanced production and farmer’s income. The subsidy, in combination with the in-house credit facilities, investment in agri-marketing and in-house capacity building, improved farmer’s accessibility to SolarNow’s agricultural product range, which otherwise would have been expensive for subsistent and emergent farmers. The program channeled the contribution by the Netherlands Embassy to farmers, in the form of an end-user subsidy on SolarNow’s agricultural product range. Thanks to the program, SolarNow has developed an agricultural product range, has launched marketing campaigns for awareness creation, and has provided pay plan facilities to clients. The investment in agri-product development, capacity building and marketing has been fully covered by SolarNow up till the end of July 2021, through third party funding from MasterCard Foundation ‘Fund for Rural Prosperity’. From July 2021 onwards, project expenditures to support promotion, awareness creation and coordination of field activities were included in the FASO project budget. 1.1. Explanation extension A first amendment to the contribution agreement was signed in June 2020, including a revised end-user subsidy amount from 25% to 35%, in an attempt to provide additional support to farmers during the COVID-19 pandemic. Furthermore, the project was extended until the 15 th November 2021, instead of the original end date 15 th November 2020, due to a less aggressive uptake of agricultural products than expected in the initial proposal. Subsequently, a second budget neutral extension was granted in December 2021, as further lock-down restrictions and related organizational changes resulted in a continuation of modest sales uptake. 1.2. Project targets for extended period The following targets were planned for the period Dec 2021 – Nov 2022: ● A total subsidy amount of EUR 101,545 to be disbursed to clients, according to table 1. ● Implementation of an awareness campaign for EUR 84,495, according to table 2. ● Monitoring development impact through impact surveys budget lines Forecast Dec '21-Nov '22 UGX Equivalent in EUR EUR conversion rate 4016.51 FASO drip kit 2,500,000 622 FASO rainmaker* 20,000,000 4,979 FASO SF2 120,000,000 29,877 FASO large water pump 120,000,000 29,877 FASO sunlight pump 140,000,000 34,856 FASO Lorentz** 3,364,508 838 FASO Milk cooler*** 1,992,000 496 total 101,545 Table 1. Annual Budget - Subsidies 3 Table 2. Annual Budget 1.3. Outline report This progress report covers the period 15 November 2021 till 15 November 2022 as well as the total results of the 4-year project (2018-2022). Chapter 2 covers the result vs the original plan of the last reporting year. Chapter 3 presents the financial report for the total project. Last, the conclusions and recommendations are discussed in chapter 4. 2. Project results 2.1. Project activities In accordance to the agreed targets and the project’s logical framework, the project was supposed to implement the following activities during the project period 15 November 2021 to 15 November 2022: ▪ Subsidy allocation of EUR 101,545 (representing 35% of the total sales value) ▪ Implementation of awareness campaigns to farmers budgeted at EUR 84,495 ▪ Monitoring progress logical framework ▪ Execution of annual impact assessment In the below sections progress on each of the activities are explained. 2.1.1 Subsidy allocation As stated in last progress report’s projections (see chapter 4.3), the following revenue generation was expected, to derive at a subsidy allocation of EUR 101,545: ● EUR 290,128 revenue generated ● EUR 101,545 subsidy allocated During reporting period Dec 2021 – Nov 2022 were: ● EUR 118,488 revenue were generated - 41% of target achieved ● EUR 37,048 subsidies were allocated - 36% of target achieved ● 50 beneficiaries were reached The results were lower than expected, but decent given the changing dynamics in the market during 2022. The biggest change in the market was the launch of the UgiFT program at the end of 2021. This World Bank program operates in almost all parts of Uganda, and targets to provide (solar) water pumping and irrigation equipment to 10,000 farmers. The funding of the program offers purchase discounts of 75% of the cost of the equipment to participating farmers. SolarNow was invited to supply equipment for this program in around 8 districts and made offers for around 700 solar water pumps. Despite the heavy discount and extensive marketing by the districts, we experienced an uptake of about 5% of the offers made. This experience reaffirmed a number of things we had 4 experienced in previous years: 1. The market for solar water pumps and irrigation equipment is still small and may be saturated for the time being. 2. Farmers’ ability to pay remains low; despite heavy discounts and extensive marketing efforts, farmers have shown to struggle with financing the balance of 25% of the required own contribution, often leading to cancellation of orders.. In addition to changing market dynamics due to new programs, SolarNow underwent further company restructuring that reduced the number of employees and branches. In summary, the challenges that were experienced: - Sector wide sales uptake has been less due to economic recession and inflationary pressures - New subsidy programs, most notably the World Bank Ugift program offered solar water pumps at up to 75% discount to farmers, reducing overall demand from the market - SolarNow’s credit facilities were put on hold, due to high default rates - SolarNow closed down its branch network due to financial constraints - SolarNow’s staff was further downsized from 104 in November 2021 to 34 staff in November 2022. Although results are lower than projected, we consider them as good achievements under the current circumstances. 2.1.2 Activities 2.1.2.1 Marketing activities Multiple awareness campaigns were implemented during the period under consideration. A brief summary of these activities as well as the associated expenditures are listed below. FASO awareness campaign 5 The farmer field day program was implemented throughout 2022, resulting in 5 organized events, visited by 490 farmers. During those events, farmers were trained on the various agri-products, its functionality, their value proposition, and a field demonstration of the equipment. Expenditure on some of the activities was a bit lower and on others a bit higher than budgeted, e.g. the radio campaigns received a bit more focus than the TV campaigns, due to their expected higher efficiency. The number of events attended was lower than budgeted which is reflected in the lower than budgeted expenditure (Eur 8,141 instead of the budgeted Eur 12,995). Overall expenditure for the awareness building and field work ended up at Eur 82,055 which was Eur 2,441 below the allocated budget for the year. 2.2 Outcomes The project was initially to deliver the following outcomes after 2 years: ▪ Total number of beneficiaries reached was expected to be 6,191 ▪ Based on the revised projections, the total number of beneficiaries reached after 3-year project implementation was expected to be approximately 4,100. ▪ Farmer’s productivity and/or income was expected to have increased with 60%. ▪ The initial agri-product contribution to SolarNow’s company revenue for the full project was expected to be 3,970,000 EUR. 2.2.1 Number of beneficiaries reached Since the projected number of beneficiaries were not realistic to achieve in a 2-year’s project, the project was extended till November 2021 and later to November 2022. Four years of implementation have resulted in: ▪ 2019: 208 clients benefited from the FASO subsidy. ▪ 2020: 498 clients benefited from the FASO subsidy. ▪ 2021: 270 clients benefited from the FASO subsidy ▪ 2022: 50 clients benefited from the FASO subsidy, for a total of 1,026 clients during the whole project Period Budgeted Actuals Variance 2019 1025 208 (817) 2020 1025 498 (527) 2021 1025 270 (755) 2022 1025 50 (975) Total 4,100 1,026 (3,074) This number is lower than expected. As discussed before, achieving sales targets was challenging. We faced many unforeseen challenges that led to a smaller number of clients buying our products. During the last 2 6 years of the project we also noted a qualitative change in the demand for pumps. Since general awareness on solar powered irrigation has increased throughout the project duration, customers requested for more customized solutions, which besides the pump could entail a water storage, distribution and irrigation design. This resulted in a more expensive solution, but with better user acceptance, product performance and longer lifespan. We generally consider this a positive trend, but also contributed further to the downward trend of the quantitative targets as is shown in the 4 year chart above. In the below table the overview of the products that we sold during the last reporting period. 2.2.2 Farmers’ impact The objective of the project is to contribute to increased productivity of farmers in terms of yield and/or income (60% increased productivity). To measure productivity, an impact survey was conducted among 35 agri-product clients. As part of this survey, clients were asked to indicate their expected increment in income, due to the investment in the subsidized agri-product. Interviews with the 35 clients have led to the following insights: Type of farmer Most clients that buy an agri-product are involved in crop farming (77%), followed by livestock (15%), domestic use (8%) Gender and age group Of all the clients that invested in an agri-product during the project period, 87% is male, while 13% is female. The largest client group that buys agri-products falls is the age group above 35 years (63%), and 37% of the agri-product clients are youth (<35yrs). 7 Productivity farmer Based on the impact survey that was conducted among 35 beneficiaries, clients have expressed that the agri-product positively affects their income. ▪ On average, crop farmers indicate a 60-70% production increment with an average increased income of UGX1,927,273 per season (EUR 494 per season). ▪ Furthermore, 18% of the clients expressed clear cost saving benefits as a result of the agri-product, with an average monthly saving of UGX 218,800, resulting in annual savings of EUR 673 per farmer. Savings were made on fuel costs, labor costs, and water bills. ▪ In the case of dairy farmers, farmers were able to increase the volume and frequency of watering their cows, leading to 58% higher milk production, resulting in a monthly income of approximately Eur 480 per farmer, a similar saving as reported in the previous year (2020-2021). 2.2.3 Company revenue In total, SolarNow was expecting to generate EUR 3,970,000 by the end of the project. Upon completion of the project the annual revenue generated with support of the FASO program was EUR 1,411,817 or 36% of the original target, broken down over the years as follows:: ▪ In 2019, SolarNow has generated UGX 1,326,849,150, equivalent to EUR 330,348. ▪ In 2020, SolarNow has generated UGX 2,179,749,615, equivalent to EUR 542,697. ▪ In 2021, SolarNow has generated UGX 1,688,074,365, equivalent to EUR 420,284. ▪ In 2022, SolarNow has generated UGX 457,529,036, equivalent to EUR 118,488. Financial Report The financial report provides a summary update on the subsidies that have been extended to the project beneficiaries. ▪ In total, the project has reached 1,026 beneficiaries between November 2018 and November 2022. ▪ During the period December 2018 to May 2020, the subsidy mechanism was a fixed percentage of 25%. From June 2020 onwards, the subsidy percentage was increased to 35%, as a Covid-19 relief measurement. Per client, a maximum of UGX 5 million subsidy per sales order was provided. ▪ The total amount of revenue generated through the sales of agri-products during this reporting year November 2021 to November 2022 was UGX 457,529,036, equivalent to EUR 118,488. ▪ The total amount of subsidy transferred to beneficiaries during this reporting year November 2021 to November 2022 was UGX 143,055,695 (equivalent to EUR 37,048). ▪ The total amount of revenue generated through the sales of agri-products during the entire project period was UGX 5,860,237,547, equivalent to EUR 1,411,817. Period Budgeted(Euros) Actuals (Euros) Variance (Euros) 2019 992,500 330,348 (662,152) 2020 992,500 542,697 (449,803) 2021 635,700 420,284 (215,416) 2022 290,129 118,488 (171,641) Total 2,910,829 1,411,817 (1,499,012) Despite not achieving the revenue targets set out at the start of the project, the Eur 1,411,817 of revenues generated for SolarNow represent a multiplier of more than 3x of the subsidy funding received. The cost savings and additional earnings to farmers are estimated to be Eur 1,045,363 per year. If we conservatively assume that these impacts will repeat for 4-5 years but deduct the investment cost, we estimate the total financial benefit created for the farmers under the FASO program is Eur 3,136,089, or Eur 3,057 per farmer (see Annex 3). With these savings and earnings added together with the revenue for SolarNow, an overall financial return of Eur 4,547,906 was generated by the FASO program. Against a total amount of Eur 454,745 of utilized subsidy, this represents a total financial return of Eur 10 for every Eur 1 that was provided as subsidy. We consider this a significant achievement and a validation that despite the lower sales output of the project, the FASO program has been a great success for both the farming community in Uganda and SolarNow as a business. 9 4. Conclusions & Lessons learned 4.1 Summary project results The below overview summarizes the project’s achievements during the period December 2018 – November 202. Note that the number of beneficiaries was revised downwards from 6,191, to 4,100. 10 4.2 Lessons learned 2018-2022 The main challenge has been achieving the projected output in terms of number of beneficiaries and the related company revenue target. The original sales projections appeared not to be realistic in light of a range of internal and external factors negatively impacting the uptake of the solar water pumps, of which the most prominent were: 1. Covid-19 extended lockdowns and related disruptions in 2020 and 2021 2. Economic headwinds resulting from the pandemic reducing financial strength of farmers 3. Restructuring of the SolarNow organization including closure of the upcountry branches, first partly and in 2022, the last year of the FASO program completely 4. Entry of new subsidy programs, most notably the World Bank UGIFT program in 2022, which had a country-wide impact and allowed farmers to access the pumps at 75% discounts. Despite the lower number of beneficiaries reached, the impact of the agri-products came out strong. The market uptake of irrigation solutions remains gradual. Despite sales figures being lower than projected, SolarNow has positioned itself on the irrigation market as the largest supplier of small-scale irrigation solutions. In addition, it has enabled substantial financial benefit for its rural customers, through additional income generation and savings from their investment. Marketing support remains important for creating awareness, which is expected to continue over the next years through various programs focused on the promotion of small solar water pumping and irrigation solutions, as well as through SolarNow’s team and partners. 11 Annex 1: Original Logical Framework Annex 2: Project Financial Summary Annex 3: Project Impact Summary Annex 4: Agricultural product portfolio 12 Annex 1. We reviewed the data of all the impact reports and extrapolated the average increase in earnings and average increase in savings by customer segment (crop farmers, dairy farmers and others). A few qualifications of the data: - The earnings were recorded in the last 3 out of 4 years by client segment (dairy, crop, other), not for the 1st year of the project. - The savings were recorded in the last 3 out of 4 years, but not separated by client segment, so the values used are the same for each segment. - Productivity data was not obtained from all farmers, but per year and per segment the average was calculated from the respondents who did provide feedback. - As the productivity surveys were only conducted during the last 3 years of the program, the calculation of total achieved earnings and savings was based on appplying the average productivity values for the last 3 years to the first cohort of customers in year 1 (see table below). This equates to an average benefit of Eur 1,019 per farmer for their first year of using the solar pump. This benefit will have been recurring for 4-5 more years, increasing the overall earnings and savings generated by the investment. Estimating the total earnings per farmer over the lifetime of the system For a full ROI analysis for the individual farmer, the cost of the systems would have to be taken into account. If we are to make an estimation of the total benefit from multi-year use of the pump, minus the investment cost, we believe that farmers that purchased pumps through FASO enjoyed a net benefit of at least 3 years of additional earnings and savings (Eur 3,057).
